segments.title: Inside Hikawa Maru's preserved engine room
segments.body: Steps lead down into the lower part of Hikawa Maru's engine room, where visitors can look closely at the machinery. The engines are well maintained, and the visitor access makes it easy to see the installation. These large diesel engines provided the power to take the ship to Seattle. The engine room alone makes the visit worthwhile.

evidence.note: The visit follows steps down into the lower engine room. The diesel engines are large and well maintained, visitors can see the machinery closely, and the engines powered the ship's voyages to Seattle.
The engine room itself is said to make the entire visit worthwhile.

segments.summary: A visit below decks shows Hikawa Maru's large diesel engines and the access that lets visitors examine the machinery closely.

segments.title: NYK Line and Seattle's growth
segments.body: The Great Northern and NYK Line illustrate the transport connections behind Seattle's growth. In this comparison, the Great Northern was probably the city's "father" when Hikawa Maru was built. A remark attributed to one of Seattle's mayors called NYK Line its "mother". NYK's ships, including Hikawa Maru, linked Seattle with the wider world and helped the city develop.

evidence.note: The Great Northern is described as probably Seattle's father, while the description of NYK Line as its mother is attributed to a Seattle mayor. NYK Line linked Seattle to the wider world and helped make the city, with ships such as Hikawa Maru providing that connection.

segments.summary: NYK Line helped Seattle grow through overseas shipping connections maintained by vessels such as Hikawa Maru.
